items.titleRaw: huggingface/transformers v5.22.0 released
items.contentRaw: ## New Models ### Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) Mistral Large 4 is Mistral's largest and most capable model to date: a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 49 billion active parameters per token (52 billion including embeddings and output layers), trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral's own datacenters in Europe. Mistral Large 4 unifies instruction following, reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows in a single set of weights. While a generalist model, it shows especially good performance on workloads such as cybersecurity, finance, and law, and it surpasses frontier closed models on visual grounding. It is natively fluent in 160+ languages, including every official language of the European Union. #### Key Features Mistral Large 4 includes the following architectural choices: - **~1T total / ~52B active parameters**: granular Mixture-of-Experts with 128 routed experts (4 active per token) and 1 shared expert. - **1M context length**, for long-context workloads. - **Multimodal input**: accepts text and image input, with text output. Pixtral-style vision encoder trained to handle variable image sizes and aspect ratios. - **Instruct and Reasoning functionalities** with function calls, reasoning effort configurable per request. Mistral Large 4 offers the following capabilities: - **Reasoning Mode**: three reasoning efforts — `low`, `medium`, `high` (default) — so the same model can answer a quick chat reply or work through a complex agentic run. - **Vision**: analyzes images, charts, technical drawings, and documents, with state-of-the-art visual grounding among open weights. - **Multilingual**: natively fluent in 160+ languages, including all official languages of the European Union. - **System Prompt**: strong adherence and support for system prompts. - **Agentic**: native function calling, JSON output, and strict JSON schema enforcement. - **Cybersecurity**: state of the art among open-weight models for security work, while refusing malicious requests. - **Large Context Window**: supports a 1M context window. The model is released under the [**Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License**](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B/blob/main/LICENSE): a modified version of the MIT license, for both commercial and non-commercial use — operating a Model-as-a-Service business requires a separate commercial license with Mistral. #### Recommended Settings - **Reasoning Effort**: - `'low'` / `'medium'` / `'high'` — default is `'high'`. - Use `reasoning_effort="high"` for complex prompts and agentic usage, `'low'` for fast chat replies and `'medium'` for day to day usage. - **Sampling**: for all reasoning efforts, we recommend the following sampling parameters: - `temperature=1.0` - `top_p=0.95` - **System Prompt**: define a clear environment and use case, including guidance on how to effectively leverage tools in agentic systems. - **Tools**: keep the set of tools well-defined and limit their number to the minimum required for the use case. - **Context**: the checkpoint supports a 1M context window. ## Breaking changes * 🚨 Separate EP logic into its own file (#49679) by @3outeille ## Quantization FP8 quantized models can now be used for adapter training (such as LoRA with PEFT). Backward passes were added to the dense and grouped FP8 matmuls, and `is_trainable` is now `True`. Backward also dequantizes experts in chunks and skips autograd at inference, which cuts peak memory in the MoE layer backward from about 28.9 GiB to 2.8 GiB at 8k tokens. Separately, the AMD CI image now install * FP8 backward: chunked expert dequant, skip autograd.Function at inference (#50117) by @ArthurZucker in [#50117] * Train adapters on top of FP8 weights (#50031) by @qgallouedec in [#50031] * [AMD CI] Install onnxscript, bitsandbytes and peft in the AMD image (#50046) by @Abdennacer-Badaoui in [#50046] ## Bugfixes and improvements * Processor unnecessary warnings (#49812) by @zucchini-nlp in [#49812] * Fix boolean padding in ClapFeatureExtractor (#23648) (#49960) by @rudy-07 in [#49960] * [Fix] Count cropping of an uninitialized layer as a no-op (#50104) by @remi-or in [#50104] * [loading] Allow `PermuteForRope` to act on single tensors while renaming (#50092) by @Cyrilvallez in [#50092] * Add Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe (#50084) by @eustlb in [#50084] * [Nemotron3Diarization] add left context support (#49283) by @eustlb in [#49283] * [Janus] Fix processor iterating a string prompt character by character (#50044) by @tarekziade in [#50044] * fix(config): forward token kwarg to get_config_dict in PreTrainedConfig.from_pretrained (#50081) by @ydshieh in [#50081] * Fix `rope_scaling` setter for configs that assign it during init (#50080) by @hmellor in [#50080] * [timesfm] Fix fp16 overflow on pad_val in _forward_transform (#50021) by @tarekziade in [#50021] * Update dev version (#50068) by @albertvillanova in [#50068] * Pin the shared Hub MIC fleet dataset (#49802) by @tarekziade in [#49802] * [docs] NVIDIA/Intel/CPU (#49650) by @stevhliu in [#49650] * Document how to handle non-persistent buffer initialization in custom models (#49880) by @Tialo in [#49880] * Remove legacy benchmark/ and disable automatic benchmark runs (#50040) by @tarekziade in [#50040] * Remove deprecation cycle for candidate generators (#50034) by @Cyrilvallez in [#50034] * Fix test pil import leak (#49915) by @guarin in [#49915] * fix: preserve NumPy integer label dtypes in default data collators (#49900) by @BlazeSR10hawk in [#49900] * [ESMFold2] Don't build the MSA encoder for checkpoints without one (#49890) by @jimburtoft in [#49890] * [minimax_m3_vl] Gate the integration tests on total accelerator memory (#50025) by @tarekziade `_init_weights` gaps in 7 audio models and enable `test_can_init_all_missing_weights` for them (#49386) * Fix image backend equivalence tests for Pillow 13 (#50105) * [Janus] Fix processor iterating a The model is released under the [**Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License**](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B/blob/main/LICENSE): a modified version of the MIT license, for both commercial and non-commercial use — operating a Model-as-a-Service business requires a separate commercial license with Mistral. #### Recommended Settings - **Reasoning Effort**: - `'low'` / `'medium'` / `'high'` — default is `'high'`. - Use `reasoning_effort="high"` for complex prompts and agentic usage, `'low'` for fast chat replies and `'medium'` for day to day usage. - **Sampling**: for all reasoning efforts, we recommend the following sampling parameters: - `temperature=1.0` - `top_p=0.95` - **System Prompt**: define a clear environment and use case, including guidance on how to effectively leverage tools in agentic systems. - **Tools**: keep the set of tools well-defined and limit their number to the minimum required for the use case. - **Context**: the checkpoint supports a 1M context window. ## Breaking changes * 🚨 Separate EP logic into its own file (#49679) by @3outeille ## Quantization FP8 quantized models can now be used for adapter training (such as LoRA with PEFT). Backward passes were added to the dense and grouped FP8 matmuls, and `is_trainable` is now `True`. Backward also dequantizes experts in chunks and skips autograd at inference, which cuts peak memory in the MoE layer backward from about 28.9 GiB to 2.8 GiB at 8k tokens. Separately, the AMD CI image now install * FP8 backward: chunked expert dequant, skip autograd.Function at inference (#50117) by @ArthurZucker in [#50117] * Train adapters on top of FP8 weights (#50031) by @qgallouedec in [#50031] * [AMD CI] Install onnxscript, bitsandbytes and peft in the AMD image (#50046) by @Abdennacer-Badaoui in [#50046] ## Bugfixes and improvements * Processor items.titleRaw: ollama/ollama v0.40.15 released
items.contentRaw:
## MiMo V2.6

Xiaomi MiMo's [mimo-v2.6](https://ollama.com/library/mimo-v2.6), a 9B model built for code and agent workflows, is now supported in Ollama.

```sh
ollama run mimo-v2.6
```

## AutoTrust decision models

[AutoTrust](https://ollama.com/library/autotrust-jev) decision models read text and return choices, yes or no probabilities, and ratings for the questions you supply. The family includes 9b, 35b, and 27b-vl sizes — the 35b and 27b-vl sizes can also read images.

```sh
ollama run autotrust-jev "A customer says their card was charged twice." --ask "Is this a billing issue?"
```

Note: autotrust-jev is supported on Apple silicon in this release.

## What's Changed

 - ollama launch now supports Kimi Code CLI — the successor to kimi-cli — and offers to migrate existing kimi-cli setups
 - ollama launch now fills in Pi's model list automatically so models can be picked inside Pi, and Claude Desktop's model
   picker shows Ollama's actual model names
 - Recurrent and vision GGUF models can now serve more than one request at a time
 - Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 models using long-context (YaRN) scaling
 - Running ollama with no arguments opens the welcome launcher

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.14...v0.40.15

items.titleRaw: ollama/ollama v0.40.14 released
items.contentRaw:
## What's Changed
* `ollama launch claude` now applies the model's output token limit for Claude Code, so cloud models no longer run into the 128k default cap
* Cloud web search responses on `/api/chat` are now decoded correctly, including compressed responses
* OpenAI-compatible endpoints no longer override a model's packaged sampler defaults — clients that send no `temperature`/`top_p` get the model's own values instead of 1.0, matching `/api/chat`
* `/v1/responses` now preserves readable input content, including prior assistant refusals, instead of flattening it
* Ollama's app can now retry ChatGPT disconnect failures instead of leaving the connection in a broken state
* `ollama launch codex` verifies ChatGPT routing before configuring, and reports a clear error when routing is unavailable
* Faster top-k sampling on MLX for large vocabularies

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.13...v0.40.14

items.titleRaw: Show HN: AgentState – Lightweight state manager for multi-agent AI workflows
items.contentRaw:
AgentState to solve a problem I kept running into: managing state for multi-agent AI systems is surprisingly hard. When you have multiple AI agents that need to coordinate, persist their state, and query each other's status, you typically end up with a mess of Redis/Postgres setups, custom queuing, and manual synchronization code.

The whole thing is ~3MB, written in Rust for performance and safety, runs in Docker, and handles 1000+ ops/sec. I've been running it in production for AI workflows and it's been rock solid.

items.titleRaw: Show HN: ML Blocks – Deploy multimodal AI workflows without code
items.contentRaw:
Hey everyone,

ML Blocks is a node-based workflow builder to create multi-modal AI workflows without writing any code.

You connect blocks that call various visual models like GPT4v, Segment Anything, Dino etc. along with basic image processing blocks like resize, invert color, blur, crop, and several others.

The idea is to make it easier to deploy multi-step image processing workflows, without needing to spin up endless custom OpenCV cloud functions to glue together AI models. Usually, even if you're using cloud inference servers like Replicate, you still need to write your own image processing code to pre and post-process images in your pipeline. When you're trying to move fast, that's just unnecessary overhead.

With ML Blocks, you can build a workflow and deploy the whole thing as a single API. AFAIK, ML Blocks is the only end-to-end workflow builder built specifically for image processing.

If you're curious, our models run on Replicate, HuggingFace & Modal Labs cloud GPUs and we use React Flow for the node UX.
